title: I Used the Insect-Pinning Station Log on the Intern Who Pocketed My Pins

parts.text: I sat at station six at 1:03 p.m. and intern Pax was already using my numbered pins. The card said: ONE STATION. TWO HOURS. PINS STAY WITH THE TRAY. I was thirty-four, collections volunteer, holding a tray that listed our series. Pax shrugged. "Interns are the tray." I photographed the card, the log, and his forceps on my foam. Then I asked for the pin sheet. At 1:11 the lab pinged why Pax's name was on my box. I kept my voice lab-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The lab can see Pax's forceps on my foam during our station.

social.video_title: He used my numbered pins on my foam — Part 1/2
social.description: Pinning station, an intern on my foam, a two-hour log he posted. I logged the forceps. Would you have asked for the pin sheet?

parts.text: Pax called it a spare until the lab asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the forceps still. The pins went back to my box. Pax ran his own two hours and told the next intern atmosphere was always about spread. Spread is a word interns use when a log exists. Station policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE TRAY. I keep our pins on a labeled tin. Pax brown-bags his jokes. The station finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
